titulo: The spec sheet for your humanoid
lead: A manufacturer spec sheet, a simulation file, and a measurement don't say the same thing, and sim-to-real lives in the difference. In this lesson you compare two Menagerie humanoids by script, build a spec sheet that separates the three sources, and leave with the study plan for the program.
objetivo: compare two Menagerie humanoids by script and build your own spec sheet, separating manufacturer, file, and measurement.

aprende.t: comparar.py: 7 items read from the file, side by side
The sheet in three columns: manufacturer, file, measurement
Which robot a lab would buy today, and why
The dated plan for the next FTH courses

hero_alt: Two mockups of humanoid robots of different heights side by side on a dark table, with a caliper and an open notebook.

secoes.sub: Each row of the sheet says where it came from. Tap each block.

nos.detalhe: What the company publishes: degrees of freedom, mass, battery, compute, price. It holds with version, source, and date; it changes and sometimes leaves things out (the G1 doesn't publish Wh or torque per joint).
What the simulation model declares: nu, mass, limits, maximum torque, sensors. It is a specific, approximate version of the robot. Cite the Menagerie folder and commit.

What you measured on the model: 31 N·m at the knee while squatting, 327 N at the feet, falls starting at 35 N. A simulation measurement holds for the model; on the real robot, only after system identification (course 2).

33.3 kg in the file × ~35 kg on the sheet; 29 degrees of freedom in the model × 23 on the base G1; 139 N·m at the model's knee × 90/120 N·m reported. Each difference is a spot where a policy trained in simulation can fail on the robot.

secoes.legenda: The "difference" column is the sim-to-real to-do list.

secoes.titulo: Which robot a lab would consider in Oct 2026
secoes.sub: With a price only when there is a source, and always varying by version and reseller. Tap each one.

texto: It is the platform that shows up in almost everything: Menagerie (29 degrees of freedom), unitree_rl_lab, mjlab, retargeting (GMR), SONIC with open weights, and LeRobot.
The base (US$ 13.5 thousand) has no SDK; the EDU, which does, is on request.
1.23 m, 27–29 kg, from 20 to 40 degrees of freedom depending on the version; US$ 4,900 to 5,900 in the official store (EDU on request).
Fewer people publish a controller for it than for the G1: less ready-made code.
95 cm, 19.5 kg, 22 degrees of freedom, 117 TOPS, 1 h 10 min walking at 1.1 m/s (official sheet). In the RoboCup 2026 program, US$ 14,999 is the public price.
The T1, from the same company, has a model in the Menagerie (booster_t1, 23 actuators); Booster's current line is T2 and K1, and the T1 may have been discontinued (uncertain).

Berkeley Humanoid Lite: 3D-printed, under US$ 5 thousand in parts (reported), with training in Isaac Lab and sim2sim validation in the repository. ToddlerBot: 30 degrees of freedom, Jetson Orin NX, public parts list.
Both need a workbench and assembly time; the simulation model comes with it.

perguntas.p: What is the "diferença" column of the spec sheet for?
opcoes: To list where the model and the robot diverge: the sim-to-real to-do list.
To choose which of the three sources to delete at the end of the sheet.
To prove that the manufacturer publishes fake numbers in the spec sheet.
For nothing, because the MJCF file alone is enough to do sim-to-real.
perguntas.explica: Different mass, degrees of freedom and torque between the file and the robot are exactly what makes the policy trained in simulation fail on the floor. Course 2 tackles that list.

perguntas.p: A lab wants the humanoid with the most open-source code ready for RL and retargeting. What does the program's research point to?
opcoes: The R1, because it is the cheapest in Unitree's store in 2026.
Any of them, because they all have the same open-source support today.
The G1 EDU: it is in Menagerie, unitree_rl_lab, mjlab, GMR and SONIC.
The Atlas, as the product humanoid launched at CES 2026.
perguntas.explica: The G1 has become the de facto reference platform. A low price (R1) does not make up for the lack of ready-made code; the Atlas 2026 batch is committed to Hyundai and Google DeepMind (reported).

perguntas.p: comparar.py says 139 N·m of maximum torque on the G1. How do you put that in the spec sheet?
opcoes: In the manufacturer column, as the official G1 specification.
In the file column, citing the Menagerie folder and commit.
In the measurement column, as torque you measured on the robot.
Nowhere: maximum torque does not belong in a spec sheet.
perguntas.explica: 139 N·m is the model's actuatorfrcrange. What was measured was the squat (31 N·m); from the manufacturer, Unitree does not publish per-joint torque on the page read.
